verses.zh: 你们务要常存弟兄相爱的心。
verses.en: Brotherly love must continue.
verses.commentary:
13:1

NASB
"Let love of the brethren continue"

NKJV, Peshitta
"Let brotherly love continue"

NRSV
"Let mutual love continue"

TEV
"Keep on loving one another as Christians"

NJB
"Continue to love one another like brothers"

This is a PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE (not a SUBJUNCTIVE, as
NASB translates), meaning "abide" or "continue" (TEV, NJB). The thing the readers are to continue is "brotherly love"
(philadelphia, cf. Rom. 12:10; 1 Thess. 4:9; 1 Pet. 3:8). They have done this in the past (cf.
Heb. 6:10; 10:32-35) and are encouraged to continue. It is a clear sign that one knows God (cf. Matt. 25:31-46; John 13:34-45;
15:12,17; 1 John 2:10; 3:11,14,17-24; 4:7-21; 2 John 5).

There are several phileō compounds in this chapter.

- brother love, Heb. 13:1

- stranger love, Heb. 13:2

- money love, Heb. 13:5

verses.zh: 不可忘记用爱心接待客旅；因为曾有接待客旅的，不知不觉就接待了天使。
verses.en: Do not neglect hospitality because through it some have entertained angels without knowing it.[NOTE:1]
notes: This is a vague allusion to people described in scripture and extra-biblical literature and may include Abraham and Sarah (Gen 18:2-15), Lot (Gen 19:1-14), Gideon (Judg 6:11-18), Manoah (Judg 13:3-22), and possibly Tobit (Tob 12:1-20).
verses.commentary:
13:2 "Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers" This is a PRESENT MIDDLE
(deponent) IMPERATIVE. It is a compound of "phileō" and "stranger" i.e., "love of
strangers." There were no motels in those days except immoral inns and they were very expensive. Christians
are called on to open their homes to itinerant ministers (cf. Matt. 25:35; Rom. 12:13; 1 Tim. 3:2; Titus 1:8;
1 Pet. 4:9; 2 John; Didache 11:4-6).

▣ "entertained angels without knowing it" This is an allusion to Genesis 18, where Abraham meets
three angels who looked like men (cf. also Tobit chapters 4-7). Angels also appeared to

- Abraham and Sarah (Genesis 18)

- Lot (Genesis 19)

- Hagar (Genesis 21)

- Gideon (Judges 6)

- Manoah (Judges 13)

- Tobit (Tob 12, non-canonical book)

This does not mean that Christians may have angels visit; but as men of old helped strangers and
received a blessing, so too, are believers to do.

verses.zh: 你们要记念被捆绑的人，好像与他们同受捆绑；也要记念遭苦害的人，想到自己也在肉身之内。
verses.en: Remember those in prison as though you were in prison with them,[NOTE:1] and those ill-treated as though you, too, felt their torment.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “as being imprisoned together.”
Or “since you too are vulnerable”; Grk “you also being in the body.”
verses.commentary:
13:3 "Remember the prisoners" This is a PRESENT MIDDLE (deponent) IMPERATIVE.
These readers had followed Christ's words of Matt. 25:44-45, for in Heb. 10:32-36 they had helped other believers.
Their imprisonment was not for evil deeds, but for their faith in Christ (cf. 1 Pet. 4:14-15). Imprisonment was a
real possibility for all early believers, as it is for many believers in today's world
also.

▣ "since you yourselves also are in the body" This could refer to

- the physical body (cf. 2 Cor. 12:2, same Greek structure), susceptible to persecution and imprisonment

- the body of Christ (although the text does not have the expected Greek ARTICLE), the
Church, which was the object of persecution

verses.zh: 婚姻，人人都当尊重，床也不可污秽；因为苟合行淫的人，　神必要审判。
verses.en: Marriage must be honored among all and the marriage bed kept undefiled, for God will judge sexually immoral people and adulterers.
verses.commentary:
13:4 "Marriage is to be held in honor among all" There is no VERB. If one supplies
an INDICATIVE, "is," then the statement is against false teaching (cf. 1 Cor. 7:38, which made
marriage morally inferior to celibacy or 1 Tim. 4:3). If one supplies an IMPERATIVE,
"Let. . .be. . .," as in NASB of Heb. 13:1, then it is an encouragement against the immoral tendencies of
pagan culture (Heb. 13:4 favors this option).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CELIBACY
AND MARRIAGE

▣ "the marriage bed is to be undefiled" Marriage is a gift from God and the norm
for all (cf. Gen. 1:28; 9:1,7). It is not sinful or shameful. The Greek philosophical concept of asceticism,
the view that the body is evil and that to deny its wants and needs show a superior spirituality, affected
the early church! And still does!

The term "undefiled" is used in Heb. 7:26 to describe the sexual purity of
Jesus, our High Priest. It was used in the Septuagint to refer to adultery.

This warning against sexual promiscuity is surprising if this book is written to Jewish people.
The Gentile culture of the first century was characterized by sexual exploitation, but not the Jewish
community. There is so much about the historical setting and recipients of Hebrews that is uncertain.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

▣ "fornicators" The term in the OT means sexual relations between two unmarried people, but in
the NT it has the wider connotation of sexual immorality of any kind. We get the English word "pornography"
from this Greek term.

▣ "adulterers"This refers to sexual relations between people, one or both of whom are married to
other people. Sexual sins were a major concern of the early church because of the rampant immorality and
worship practices of pagan culture (cf. Gal. 5:19-21; Eph. 5:1-14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ADULTERY

▣ "God will judge" God's judgment of improper human sexuality can be seen in Rom. 1:24-32;
Gal. 5:19-21; Eph. 4:19; Col. 3:5; Rev. 21:8; 22:15. However, there are other passages like 1 Cor. 5:5 and
1 Tim. 1:9-11, which relate to believers who commit these immoral acts. The early church had to face
immorality in the lives of believers and try to draw some guidelines.

- they need to repent

- other believers are to help them (cf. Gal. 6:1; James 5:16,19-20)

- believers are not to be "best" friends with immoral believers (cf. 1 Cor. 5:9-13)

The Christian witness of morality, strong marriages, hospitality, and brotherly love are as crucial
today as in the first century.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGE, JUDGMENT, JUSTICE

verses.zh: 你们存心不可贪爱钱财，要以自己所有的为足；因为主曾说：「我总不撇下你，也不丢弃你。」
verses.en: Your conduct must be free from the love of money, and you must be content with what you have, for he has said, “I will never leave you and I will never abandon you.”[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Deut 31:6, 8.
verses.commentary:
13:5

NASB
"Make sure that your character is free from the love of money"

NKJV
"Let your conduct be without covetousness"

NRSV, TEV
"keep your lives free from the love of money"

NJB
"Put avarice out of your lives"

Peshitta
"Do not be carried away by the love of money"

There is no VERB, again an IMPERATIVE is implied. The
NOUN is a compound of

- an ALPHA PRIVATIVE (which negates)

- phileō ( the third compound with phileō since Heb. 13:1), to love

- a silver coin

It means "not a lover of money." The problem is not the money, but the love of money (cf.
Luke 12:15; 16:14; 1 Tim. 3:3; 6:10,17-19; 2 Tim. 3:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

▣ "being content with what you have" This is a PRESENT PASSIVE PARTICIPLE used in
an IMPERATIVAL sense. This is a key issue for happiness. It is a worldview that does not focus
on the physical and the immediate. Contentment is a wonderful gift from God that must be accepted by faith
and lived out daily (cf. 2 Cor. 9:8; Phil. 4:11-12; 1 Tim. 6:6-10).

▣ "I will never desert you, nor will I ever forsake you" This is a
loose quote with two emphatic DOUBLE NEGATIVES, taken from God's promises to His leaders and
people. God is with us and for us (cf. Deut. 31:6-8; Josh. 1:5; 1 Chr. 28:20; Isa. 41:10,13,14,17). Believers
do not have to fear for daily provisions (cf. Matt. 6:19-34).

verses.zh: 所以我们可以放胆说：主是帮助我的，我必不惧怕；人能把我怎么样呢？
verses.en: So we can say with confidence, “The Lord is my helper, and[NOTE:1] I will not be afraid. What can people do to me?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Some significant mss (א* C* P 0285vid 33 1175 1739 lat) lack καί (kai), but because the omission conforms to the wording of Ps 118:6 (117:6 LXX), it is suspect.
A quotation from Ps 118:6.
verses.commentary:
13:6 "The Lord" This is a quote from the Septuagint of Ps. 118:6, but this
same truth is also found in Psalm 56:4,11.

▣ "The Lord is my helper" Psalm 118 is a powerful word of confidence
in God's love, forgiveness, presence, and help.

The NOUN "helper" is used only here in the NT (but the VERB is
in Heb. 2:18), but is used often in the LXX. It means "to give aid," "to come to one's rescue."

▣ "What will man do to me" This great truth (cf. Ps. 56:4,11; 118:6)
is also stated in slightly different terms in Rom. 8:31b and then illustrated in Rom. 8:32-39.

verses.zh: 从前引导你们、传　神之道给你们的人，你们要想念他们，效法他们的信心，留心看他们为人的结局。
verses.en: Remember your leaders, who spoke God’s message to you; reflect on the outcome of their lives and imitate their faith.
verses.commentary:
13:7 "Remember" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE. The implication is to pray for the
church leaders and honor them! This is a different, but similar, word from Heb. 13:3. Believers need to be conscious
of the need for praying for and honoring their leaders' loving service to the body of Christ (cf. Heb. 13:3)
and her leaders (cf. Heb. 13:7,17,24; 1 Thess. 5:12-13).

Guidelines on how to "remember" faithful leaders.

- show hospitality, v. 2

- pray for imprisoned leaders, v. 3

- honor leaders, v. 7 (cf. 1 Thess. 5:12-13)

- watch out for false teachers/leaders

- sexual exploitation, v. 4

- financial exploitation, v. 5

- strange teaching, v. 9

- obey, v. 17 (cf. 1 Cor. 16:16)

- pray for the author, v. 18

▣ "those who led you" Verses 17 and 24 deal with current leaders, so Heb. 13:7 must refer to
those leaders who first preached the gospel, but are now dead.

▣ "who spoke the word of God to you" This is the task of Christian leaders. They do not teach or
preach their discoveries or personal/cultural preferences, but the gospel of Jesus Christ. For this we honor
them, respect them, and pray for them.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

▣ "considering the result of their conduct" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE PARTICIPLE used
as an IMPERATIVE. These leaders, like those in the roll call of the faithful in chapter 11,
remained faithful during life and until death. Their lives witnessed to the validity of their messages.

▣ "imitate their faith" This is a PRESENT MIDDLE (deponent) IMPERATIVE.
Our author is calling on his readers to mimic the faith of their leaders. Paul often encourages believers to
imitate his faith (cf. 1 Cor. 4:16; 11:1-2; Phil. 3:17; 4:9; 1 Thess. 1:6; 2 Thess. 3:7,9).

verses.zh: 耶稣基督昨日、今日、一直到永远，是一样的。
verses.en: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever!
verses.commentary:
13:8 "Jesus. . .same" The OT characters of chapter 11 were good examples; the former and current
leaders were good examples; Christ is our supreme example. His character and faithfulness never change
(cf. Ps. 102:26-27, quoted in Heb. 1:12; also note James 1:17). This same theological statement is made
concerning YHWH in Mal. 3:6. God's character and mercy are constant and, so too, are Jesus Christ's. This unchangingness
should also characterize faithful followers. This unchangingness should also characterize faithful followers.

verses.zh: 你们不要被那诸般怪异的教训勾引了去；因为人心靠恩得坚固才是好的，并不是靠饮食。那在饮食上专心的从来没有得着益处。
verses.en: Do not be carried away by all sorts of strange teachings.[NOTE:1] For it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not ritual meals,[NOTE:2] which have never benefited those who participated in them.
notes: Grk “by diverse and strange teachings.”
Grk “foods,” referring to the meals associated with the OT sacrifices (see the contrast with the next verse; also 9:9-10; 10:1, 4, 11).
verses.commentary:
13:9 "Do not be carried away" This is a PRESENT PASSIVE IMPERATIVE with a
NEGATIVE PARTICLE which usually means to stop an act already in process. Some of the hearers
were contemplating "shrinking back" (cf. Heb. 2:1; 10:38). The PASSIVE VOICE implies the
activity of Satan or the demonic.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSONAL EVIL

▣ "by varied and strange teachings" Exactly what this involved is uncertain, but a similar
combination of Jewish and pagan practices is condemned in Col. 2:16-23.

It almost seems to me that parts of chapter 13 are a Pauline close, added to a letter to a synagogue written by another person.
Parts of this chapter fit a mixed-church setting, not a synagogue.

▣

NASB
"for it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace"

NKJV
"For it is good that the heart be established by grace"

NRSV
"for it is well for the heart to be strengthened by grace"

TEV
"It is good to receive inner strength from God's grace"

NJB
"it is better to rely on grace for inner strength"

Peshitta
"For it is a good thing to strengthen our hearts with grace"

This is a PRESENT PASSIVE INFINITIVE. These hearers need to be firmly
established, not on ritual, animal sacrifice or food laws (i.e., the Mosaic Covenant), but on the undeserved, unmerited grace of God in
Jesus Christ (i.e., the New Covenant, cf. Heb. 13:7). They were vacillating between Moses and Jesus. Jesus, the
unchanging Word of the Father, is far superior to the procedures and words of the first covenant (i.e., Matt. 5:31-32; 12:8; Mark 2:28; 7:15,19;
Luke 6:5).

Understanding God's unchanging character and love, so clearly expressed in the life, teaching,
and death of Jesus (the gospel), is what gives believers encouragement. Believers' hearts and minds are
strengthened through a knowledge of the gospel and a personal relationship with the Great Shepherd, not
through external rituals and procedures (the old Mosaic covenant) but through faith.

▣ "heart" This author often addresses the spiritual issue of the "heart." He quotes several OT texts.

- Heb. 3:8,15; 4:7, "do not harden your hearts" (Ps. 95:8)

- Heb. 3:10, "go astray in their hearts" (Ps. 95:10)

- Heb. 8:10, "write them upon their hearts" (Jer. 31:33)

He then summarizes these truths in Heb. 3:12; 4:12, and 10:22. The heart represents the mental,
emotional, and volitional aspects of mankind. Christianity deals with the internal needs of fallen humanity,
whereas Judaism could not.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

▣ "not by foods, through which those who were so occupied were not benefitted" This is a reference to

- Leviticus 11. The food laws had passed away in Christ (cf. Matt. 15:11; Mark 7:18-23; Acts 10; Col. 2:16-23). They
were no longer binding on believers for salvation (cf. Galatians 3; Acts 15), but in a church setting, believers were still
to be conscious of "weaker brothers" (cf. Acts 15:19-20; Rom. 14:1-15:6; 1 Corinthians 8; 10:23-33) and to try not to
offend their weak consciences.

- The sacrifices where the worshiper got to eat part of the animal.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOOD LAWS

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE OFFERING

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRISTIAN FREEDOM vs. CHRISTIAN RESPONSIBILITY

verses.zh: 我们有一祭坛，上面的祭物是那些在帐幕中供职的人不可同吃的。
verses.en: We have an altar that those who serve in the tabernacle have no right to eat from.
verses.commentary:
13:10 "We have an altar" The analogy seems to be a spiritual (heavenly) tabernacle, not a physical
altar and, therefore, it refers to Jesus' sacrificial work on behalf of believers. It is a powerful image
of our access to God through Christ.

▣ "no right to eat" This is another allusion to Leviticus 16. Believers in Jesus have access to a superior
altar that the OT Levites could not approach.

verses.zh: 原来牲畜的血被大祭司带入圣所作赎罪祭；牲畜的身子被烧在营外。
verses.en: For the bodies of those animals whose blood the high priest brings[NOTE:1] into the sanctuary as an offering for sin are burned outside the camp.
notes: Grk “whose blood is brought by the high priest.”
verses.commentary:
13:11 "as an offering for sin, are burned outside the camp" This is another allusion to the
procedures of Lev. 16:27-the Day of Atonement.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL, I. E. #2

verses.zh: 所以，耶稣要用自己的血叫百姓成圣，也就在城门外受苦。
verses.en: Therefore, to sanctify the people by his own blood, Jesus also suffered outside the camp.
verses.commentary:
13:12 "Jesus. . .suffered outside the gate" This is a rabbinic word play as the OT sacrifices were
taken outside of the camp, Jesus was taken outside the city of Jerusalem to be crucified.

▣ "sanctify" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

verses.zh: 这样，我们也当出到营外，就了他去，忍受他所受的凌辱。
verses.en: We must go out to him, then, outside the camp, bearing the abuse he experienced.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “his abuse.”
verses.commentary:
13:13 "So, let us go out to Him" This is a key verse in the book. It is a PRESENT MIDDLE
(deponent) SUBJUNCTIVE, which speaks of continuous action and adds an element of contingency
(this is the final admonition and warning against "shrinking back"). Believers need to publicly identify with
Him and bear His reproach regardless of the consequences (cf. Rom. 8:17; 2 Cor. 1:5,7; Phil. 3:10; 1 Pet. 4:13). This
is the clear call for these "sheltered" synagogue believers to move into the full light of Great Commission Christianity
(cf. Matt. 28:19-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8).

verses.zh: 我们在这里本没有常存的城，乃是寻求那将来的城。
verses.en: For here we have no lasting city, but we seek the city that is to come.
verses.commentary:
13:14 "the city" This is imagery for heaven using the Israelite capital in the Promised Land
(cf. Heb. 11:10,16; 12:22; John 14:2). This same type of imagery is seen in Heb. 11:14, "a country."

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO "CITIES"
IN ISAIAH

verses.zh: 我们应当靠着耶稣，常常以颂赞为祭献给　神，这就是那承认主名之人嘴唇的果子。
verses.en: Through him then let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, acknowledging his name.
verses.commentary:
13:15 "Through Him" This refers to Jesus, mentioned by name in Heb. 13:12, who sanctified His people by
the sacrifice of His own blood outside the gate of Jerusalem. All spiritual benefits come through Him! He is our only
access to God (cf. John 14:6; Acts 4:12; 1 Tim. 2:5; 1 John 5:10-12).

▣ "let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE
SUBJUNCTIVE. The sacrificial system, given to Israel to promote fellowship with God by dealing with
the sin problem, involved five types of sacrifices.

- Two were mandatory

- the "sin offering"; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN OFFERING

- the "trespass or guilt" offering; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GUILT OFFERING

- Three were voluntary

- wholly burnt offering; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: BURNT OFFERINGS

- grain/meal offering; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GRAIN OFFERING

- fellowship, or peace, offering; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE OFFERING

It is in connection with these last three that the concept of thanksgiving and praise are mentioned
(cf. Lev. 7:12). These sacrifices are described in detail in Leviticus 1-7. The Psalms mention this aspect of
adoration often (cf. Ps. 27:6;50:14; 69:30; 107:22; 116:17). The phrase "sacrifice of praise" comes from the
Septuagint (cf. Lev. 7:2,3,5; 2 Chr. 29:31; 33:16; Ps. 50:14,23; 107:22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SACRIFICIAL SYSTEMS OF THE ANE

▣ "praise" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONFESSION/PROFESSION

▣ "the fruit of lips" This phrase reflects Isa. 57:19 and Hosea 14:2 from the Septuagint. Passages
like this were used by the Israelites in exile to substitute verbal praise in place of animal sacrifices
because they had no access to the temple in Jerusalem. The temple was totally destroyed in 586 B.C. by Nebuchadnezzar II, the
neo-Babylonian king. It was destroyed again by Rome in A.D. 70. There has been no place for Jews to offer sacrifices
since A.D. 70. Modern Judaism uses verses like these to advocate verbal sacrifices.

The date of the writing of this book is uncertain (see Introduction, Date).

▣

NASB
"that give thanks to His name"

NKJV, Peshitta
"giving thanks to His name"

NRSV
"that confess his name"

TEV
"that confess him as Lord"

NJB
"those who acknowledge his name"

For believers our praise to God is our confession (homologēo) of Jesus (using
His name as in Matt. 28:19-20 or Rom. 10:9-13) as Lord (cf. TEV, which reflects Phil. 2:6-11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONFESS/PROFESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE NAME OF THE LORD (NT)

verses.zh: 只是不可忘记行善和捐输的事，因为这样的祭是　神所喜悦的。
verses.en: And do not neglect to do good and to share what you have,[NOTE:1] for God is pleased with such sacrifices.
notes: Grk “neglect doing good and fellowship.”
verses.commentary:
13:16 "And do not neglect doing good" This is a PRESENT MIDDLE IMPERATIVE with a
NEGATIVE PARTICLE, which usually means to stop an act in progress. God is pleased when His
children love and help each other (cf. Phil. 4:18 and Eph. 2:10).

In a Jewish context this "good things" probably refers to almsgiving (cf. Matt. 6:1), a weekly
gift of money given by members of the synagogue to purchase food for the needy. The Jews considered this an
act of righteousness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ALMSGIVING

▣ "for with such sacrifices God is pleased" Notice in Heb. 13:15 the acceptable sacrifice was
professed faith in Christ; now it is Christlike living. The gospel is surely both! We must never separate justification from
sanctification.

verses.zh: 你们要依从那些引导你们的，且要顺服；因他们为你们的灵魂时刻警醒，好像那将来交帐的人。你们要使他们交的时候有快乐，不致忧愁；若忧愁就与你们无益了。
verses.en: Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they keep watch over your souls and will give an account for their work.[NOTE:1] Let them do this[NOTE:2] with joy and not with complaints, for this would be no advantage for you.
notes: Or “as ones who will give an account”; Grk “as giving an account.”
Grk “that they may do this.”
verses.commentary:
13:17 "Obey. . .submit" This is a PRESENT PASSIVE (A. T. Robertson lists it as a
MIDDLE VOICE IMPERATIVE) and PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE. Although individuals are
free in Christ we must yield ourselves to spiritual authority for growth and service (cf. Heb. 13:7;
1 Cor. 16:16; 1 Thess. 5:12-13).

This word of encouragement to submit to Christian leaders is much needed in our day of
disrespect for authority of any kind, and an overemphasis on the rights and powers of the individual. God has
placed some as leaders among His people (note Num. 16:3-5). We honor them because of their call, training,
commitment, and service. However, there is an opposite "ditch." God's calling has been abused by some
authoritarian personalities. There must be a balance, a mutual respect, a co-operative spirit between God's
people and God's leaders. All believers are called to be subject to one another out of respect for Christ
(cf. Eph. 5:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SUBMISSION

▣ "they keep watch" This term means "to be awake," "to be vigilant" (cf. Mark 13:33; Luke 21:36;
Eph. 6:18), which is imagery for diligent watchfulness and service (cf. Isa. 62:6; Ezek. 3:17; 33:7-9).

▣ "as those who will give an account" Leaders are responsible for their ministry and will give an
account to God (cf. 1 Cor. 3:10-15). They are stewards!

▣ "Let them do this with joy and not with grief" The attitude of the congregation does not
determine the ministry, but it does make the process enjoyable or painful.

verses.zh: 请你们为我们祷告，因我们自觉良心无亏，愿意凡事按正道而行。
verses.en: Pray for us, for we are sure that we have a clear conscience and desire to conduct ourselves rightly in every respect.
verses.commentary:
13:18 "Pray for us" Prayer by leadership (cf. James 4:1-4) and for leadership is crucial (cf. Eph. 6:18-19; Phil. 4:6;
1 Thess. 5:25; 1 Tim. 2:1-2,8). The PLURAL may refer to a ministry group including Timothy
(cf. Heb. 13:23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

▣ "for we are sure that we have a good conscience, desiring to conduct ourselves honorably in all
things" Attitude and lifestyle set the foundation for leadership. The author of Hebrews has mentioned the
"conscience" several times (cf. Heb. 9:9,14; 10:2,22; 13:18). The power of Jesus' redemption and the
indwelling Spirit has removed the fear of God and shame of past sins and replaced them with a joy, peace,
confidence, not in human performance, but in the gospel! This knowledge of the gospel is the helmet of
salvation (cf. Eph. 6:17; 1 Thess. 5:8).

Some commentators have seen this verse as relating to some type of accusations being leveled at
the author (similar to Paul's situation in 1 Corinthians and Galatians).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSCIENCE

verses.zh: 我更求你们为我祷告，使我快些回到你们那里去。
verses.en: I especially ask you to pray[NOTE:1] that I may be restored to you very soon.
notes: Grk “I urge you to do this all the more.”
verses.commentary:
13:19 This is a rather cryptic verse. Somehow the author's coming was related to their prayers. This
sounds so much like Paul (cf. Philemon 22). Prayer releases God's effective power for ministry. Believers'
prayers affect God and others.

Some commentators (e.g., H. E. Dana's Jewish Christianity, p. 268) have assumed this
refers to the author's sickness, or even imprisonment (the term "sooner" is also used of Timothy in
Heb. 13:23).

verses.zh: 但愿赐平安的　神，就是那凭永约之血、使群羊的大牧人―我主耶稣从死里复活的　神，
verses.en: Now may the God of peace who by the blood of the eternal covenant brought back from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep, our Lord Jesus,
verses.commentary:
13:20 "Now the God of peace" This title for God the Father is used only here and in Paul's writings
(cf. Rom. 15:33; 16:20; 1 Cor. 14:33; 2 Cor. 13:11; Phil. 4:9; 1 Thess. 5:23; and the title "Lord of Peace" 2 Thess. 3:16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DESCRIPTIVE TITLES FOR GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (NT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT)

▣ "who brought up from the dead" The NT normally depicts God the Father as raising Jesus from the
dead (cf. Acts 2:24; 3:15; 4:10; 5:30; 10:40; 13:30,33,34,37; 17:31; Rom. 6:4,9; 10:9; 1 Cor. 6:14;
2 Cor. 4:14; Gal. 1:1; Eph. 1:20; Col. 2:12; 1 Thess. 1:10). This shows the Father's acceptance of Jesus'
life, teachings, and sacrifice. However, there are other texts which assert the agency of the resurrection was
the Spirit (cf. Rom. 8:11) or the Son Himself (cf. John 2:19-22; 10:17-18). Theologically speaking, all three
persons of the Trinity are active in all the redemptive acts.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RESURRECTION

▣ "the great Shepherd" The term "shepherd" is OT imagery for

- YHWH (cf. Gen. 49:24; Ps. 23:1; 78:52; 80:1; Eccl. 12:11; Isa. 40:11; 63:11; Jer. 31:10; Ezekiel 34)

- the leadership of His people (cf. Jer. 10:21; 50:6-7; Ezek. 34:2-3; Zech. 11:3,5,15,17)

- the coming Messiah, son of David (cf. Ps. 78:70-72; Ezek. 34:23-24; 37:24; Micah 5:4; 7:14; Zech. 13:7;
John 10:2,11,14; 1 Pet. 2:25; 5:4)

Several times in the OT (cf. Num. 27:17; 1 Kgs. 22:17; 2 Chr. 18:16; Ezek. 34:5; Zech. 10:2) God's
people are described as scattered and without a shepherd, but now the Great Shepherd has come. He has
delivered us and is with us!

▣ "through the blood" This refers to His sinless life given which inaugurated the New Covenant (cf.
Zech. 9:11; Mark 14:24; 1 Cor. 11:25).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLOOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPRINKLED WITH BLOOD

▣ "the eternal covenant" It is difficult to sort out the different "eternal" covenants because

- As Hebrews shows, the Mosaic covenant was conditional and because of human weakness, not eternal. The OT
records conditional and unconditional covenants (i.e., the Exodus, Gen. 15:17-21).

- The covenant with Abraham (i.e., Gen. 12:1-3), whereby all the nations would be blessed, is unconditional (i.e., everlasting covenant),
and thereby, eternal (cf. Genesis 17:7,13,19; Psalm 105:9-10).

- The covenant with David, first revealed in 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17, is a foreshadowing of the Messiah, son of David,
which is unconditional, and thereby, eternal (cf. Ps. 89:3-4).

- The New Covenant is mentioned as a promised new day of righteousness (new age of the Spirit) for God's people
(cf. Isa. 55:3; 59:21; 61:8; Jer. 31:33; 32:40; 50:5; Ezek. 16:60; 37:26).

One can see how the Jews of Jesus' day were shocked at His message. He had always been God's plan of
redemption, but the failure of Israel to keep God's law given to Moses showed the need of another way of fellowship with God
other than human performance (cf. Galatians 3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 在各样善事上成全你们，叫你们遵行他的旨意；又藉着耶稣基督在你们心里行他所喜悦的事。愿荣耀归给他，直到永永远远。阿们！
verses.en: equip you with every good thing to do his will, working in us[NOTE:1] what is pleasing before him through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever.[NOTE:2] Amen.
notes: Some mss (C P Ψ 6 629* 630 1505 pm latt syh) read ὑμῖν (humin, “in you”) here, but ἡμῖν (hēmin) has stronger external support (P46 א A Dvid K 0243 0285 33 81 104 326 365 629c 1175 1739 1881 pm syp co). It is also more likely that ἡμῖν would have been changed to ὑμῖν in light of the “you” which occurs at the beginning of the verse than vice versa.

‡ Most mss (א A [C*] 0243 0285 33 1739 1881 M latt) include the words “and ever” here, but the shorter reading (supported by P46 C3 D Ψ 6 104 365 1505 al) is preferred on internal grounds. It seemed more likely that scribes would assimilate the wording to the common NT doxological expression “for ever and ever,” found especially in the Apocalypse (cf., e.g., 1 Tim 1:17; 2 Tim 4:18; Rev 4:9; 22:5) than to the “forever” of Heb 13:8. Nevertheless, a decision is difficult here. NA28 places the phrase in brackets, indicating doubts as to its authenticity.
verses.commentary:
13:21

NASB
"equip you in every good thing"

NKJV
"make you complete in every good work"

NRSV
"make you complete in everything good"

TEV
"provide you with every good thing"

NJB
"prepare you. . .in every kind of good action"

Peshitta
"make you perfect in every good work"

This VERB (katartizō, a rare AORIST ACTIVE OPTATIVE,
which is an expressed wish or desire) means to make someone or something completely adequate, sufficient, or
fully qualified (cf. Luke 6:40; 1 Cor. 1:10; 2 Cor. 13:11; 1 Thess. 3:10; 1 Pet. 5:10). Theologically this is
parallel to Eph. 2:10. God's will is that believers are conformed to the image of Jesus (cf. Rom. 8:29),
resulting in godly living which attracts the lost to Christ.

▣ "to do His will" Jesus did the Father's will in coming as the Suffering Servant (cf. Heb. 10:7).
Now His followers are called on to also do His will (cf. Heb. 10:36).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WILL (thelēma) OF GOD

▣

NASB, NRSV, REB, TEV, Peshitta, NJB
"in us"

NKJV
"in you"

NKJV's PRONOUN is found in MSS C, P, and matching the PRONOUN
at the beginning of the verse.

However, the PRONOUN "us" is found in MSS P46, א,
A, D, K, M, which is a better Greek tradition. the UBS4 gives "us" an A Rating (certain).

▣ "to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen" This phrase, so common in Paul's and Peter's
writings, is ambiguous.

- Sometimes it refers to God the Father (cf. Rom. 11:36; Eph. 3:21; 1 Pet. 4:11; 5:11; Jude v. 25; Rev. 1:6; 7:12).

- Sometimes it refers to Jesus the Son (cf. 2 Tim. 4:18; 2 Pet. 3:18).

- Sometimes it refers to both (cf. Rom. 16:27; 1 Tim. 1:17; Rev. 5:13 and here).

Often NT authors use the same titles, actions, and phrases
to describe both the Father and the Son as a way of asserting the equality and Deity of Jesus of Nazareth.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER (GREEK
IDIOM)

▣ "Amen" The original Hebrew term meant "to be firm." This developed into imagery for faithfulness, dependability,
and trustworthiness (cf. Hab. 2:4). It came to be used in the sense of "I affirm" or "I agree with" a particular statement.

SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN

verses.zh: 弟兄们，我略略写信给你们，望你们听我劝勉的话。
verses.en: Now I urge you, brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] bear with my message of exhortation, for in fact I have written to you briefly.
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 2:11.
verses.commentary:
13:22-24 The closing verses, 22-24, are similar to the way Paul closes his letters penned by a scribe,
where he takes the pen and adds a small personal note and blessing.

13:22 "I urge you" The author calls his book "a word of exhortation." He urges his readers often (cf.
Heb. 3:13; 10:25; 12:15; 13:15,22). They are brothers (and sisters) in Christ, but they must cling to Him,
follow Him, serve Him!

▣ "bear with this word of exhortation" This is a PRESENT MIDDLE IMPERATIVE, which
emphasizes the involvement of the subject and commands continual listening. The phrase "word of exhortation"
is used in Acts 13:15 for a synagogue sermon. Many believe this is what Hebrews originally was, but was
modified to become a letter.

verses.zh: 你们该知道，我们的兄弟提摩太已经释放了；他若快来，我必同他去见你们。
verses.en: You should know that[NOTE:1] our brother Timothy has been released. If he comes soon, he will be with me when I see you.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “Know that” (an imperative).
Grk “has been released, with whom, if he comes soon, I will see you.”
verses.commentary:
13:23 "brother Timothy" When Paul uses "brother," the person's name always comes first (cf. Rom. 16:23;
1 Cor. 1:1; 16:12; 2 Cor. 1:1; 2:13; Phil. 2:25). This is a key evidence against Paul's authorship. The
mentioning of Timothy reveals a time frame for the book's composition, during Paul's lifetime or soon after
his death (A.D. 64-68), but before Timothy's death.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TIMOTHY

▣ "has been released" This is a PERFECT PASSIVE PARTICIPLE. We know nothing from
Scriptures or elsewhere of Timothy being in prison. In his Word Pictures in the New Testament, p. 451,
A. T. Robertson asserts that Timothy was put in prison when he came to visit Paul, mentioned in 2 Tim.
4:11,21.

The word "released" (PERFECT PASSIVE PARTICIPLE) is used in

- Matt. 27:15; John 19:10; Acts 3:13; 4:21,23; 5:40 for release from prison

- Acts 13:3, as imagery for a release from a ministry assignment, and it may mean that here

▣ "if he comes soon, I will see you" This may imply that the author of Hebrews worked and traveled
with Timothy.

verses.zh: 请你们问引导你们的诸位和众圣徒安。从意大利来的人也问你们安。
verses.en: Greetings to all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy send you greetings.
verses.commentary:
13:24 "saints" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: SAINTS

▣ "those from Italy greet you" This phrase could mean

- the author is in Italy

- the author is from Italy

- part of the author's missionary team was from Italy

- the author is writing to Italy

In Jewish Christianity, H. A. Dana says that this verse implies that the letter was written
to the Jewish faction of the church at Rome. The first mention of the book of Hebrews was by Clement of Rome
about A.D. 97 (p. 270). However, I think it was sent to a Jewish synagogue (possibly in Rome)
that had believers as members. The warnings are directed to two groups.

- the believing Jewish group (the "you" of chapter 6), for them not to "shrink back" (cf. Heb. 10:38)

- the unbelieving group (the "those" of chapter 6) to profess/confess Jesus as the Messiah and for both
groups to fully embrace Christianity

verses.zh: 愿恩惠常与你们众人同在。阿们！
verses.en: Grace be with you all.[NOTE:1]
notes: Most witnesses, including several significant ones (א2 A C D H Ψ 0243 1739 1881 M lat sy bo), conclude the letter with ἀμήν (amēn, “amen”). Such a conclusion is routinely added by scribes to NT books because a few of these books originally had such an ending (cf. Rom 16:27; Gal 6:18; Jude 25). A majority of Greek witnesses have the concluding ἀμήν in every NT book except Acts, James, and 3 John (and even in these books, ἀμήν is found in some witnesses). It is thus a predictable variant. Further, there is sufficient testimony (P46 א* Ivid 6 33 sa) for the lack of the particle, rendering its omission the preferred reading.
verses.commentary:
13:25 This is a typical Pauline closing greeting (cf. Col. 4:18; 1 Tim. 6:21; 2 Tim. 4:22; Titus 3:15).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- If Hebrews is a letter, which appears certain from chapter 13, why is there no opening greeting?

- Does chapter 13 reflect the Jewish unbelievers or false teachers?

- What does this chapter say about Christian "leaders"?

- How does verse 23 date the book of Hebrews?

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare

the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Several things in this context do not fit the "supposed" historical setting used in this commentary
(i.e., letter addressed to a synagogue of believing Jews and unbelieving Jews, R. E. Glaze, Jr., No
Easy Salvation).

- admonition to Christians

- admonition apparently to previous pagans, not Jews

If this letter is written to a Christian group, it has the most severe warnings in the NT.
Chapter 13 seems to refer to a different group than chapters 1-12. I do not know how to answer this problem.

- This last chapter has several Pauline features.

- This chapter may have been added later to a synagogue sermon (i.e., chapters 1-11), but there is no
MSS support for this theory.
